title: Standard Practices — Release of the Chromate-Free Sealant System for Pressurised Fuselage Joints
abstract: Information bulletin releasing the chromate-free sealant system into operator repair procedures and changing the material call-out in the spares catalogue, with no aircraft work required.

sections.planning_reason: The authorisation to use hexavalent chromium in the sealant family applied to pressurised joints expires within the planning horizon of the programme, and operators need the qualified replacement in their own procedures before their existing stock runs out. Every repair using the chromated system also generates controlled waste at the operator's facility, which several customers have raised as a cost they cannot pass on. This bulletin exists to release the practice, not to change any aircraft.
sections.description: The bulletin releases the chromate-free sealant system for use at pressurised fuselage lap joints, at the joint land and at every fastener installed wet, and gives the changed application window and the compatibility statement for a chromate-free bead applied against a chromated bead already on the aircraft.
sections.accomplishment_summary: There is no aircraft work. Update the operator repair procedures to call the chromate-free system in place of the chromated system at pressurised fuselage joints. Note the application window, which shortens from four hours to ninety minutes after abrasion, and re-plan any line repair procedure that assumed the longer window. Order the re-specified hardware, namely the bolts ZEDE604998-69 and HE139604-23, the washers EN149290-27, the screws WES848069-85 and the cable ties LN455787K4, all of which carry the new surface treatment. Revise the waste handling instruction to the new disposal classification for removed material. Record acknowledgement of this bulletin in the operator quality system.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to all CIRRANE-11 and CIRRANE-13 aircraft. There is no pre-modification or post-modification condition, since existing sealant in place is not removed and a mixed joint is permitted. Aircraft from MSN C00680 onward are built with the chromate-free system throughout.
sections.material_note: There is no kit. The re-specified hardware is available from the normal spares channel. Operators holding stock of the chromated system may use it until exhausted, subject to their own local regulation on hexavalent chromium.

type_data.compliance_time: Before the operator's stock of the chromated sealant system is exhausted, and in any case before the date on which local regulation prohibits its use.
